title: Ada and the Bridge
premise: In the river city of Vellmark, apprentice clockmaker Sable Dravenmoor is summoned to repair the observatory's master clock just as winter closes the bridge — the only road out — and an occupying army settles in to wait out the armistice negotiations. Hidden inside the clock's housing he finds Ada Voss's testimony: a ledger of atrocities recorded by a murdered court clerk, whose daughter Ada is living under a false name among the occupiers' clerks. As Sable and Ada race to authenticate the record and smuggle it past the victors' historians — who intend to write the town's complicity out of existence — Sable must abandon the silences that kept him safe for twelve years and testify to what he witnessed as a child. The armistice hangs on whether truth can be entered into the record before the ink dries; the novel ends with Sable speaking his name aloud at the provisional tribunal while Ada's ledger becomes the official account, and the bridge reopens onto a town that must now live with its memory.
about_author: Ines Winterbourne is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing occupation-era records in Central European municipal collections. She writes historical fiction about ordinary people who keep accounts — literal and moral — that empires would prefer to lose.

chapters.title: The Weight of Small Gears
chapters.summary: Sable Dravenmoor, POV. Sable crosses to the observatory district for the first time in years, cataloguing the city's silences as he goes. He accepts the commission to repair the master clock, telling himself it is only work. Emotional beat: the practiced comfort of being unnoticed, already fraying.

chapters.title: Summons
chapters.summary: Sable, POV. The observatory's aging keeper, Herr Brandt, explains the clock stopped the night the clerk Elias Voss died — twelve years ago. Sable notices the coincidence but says nothing. Beat: unease disguised as professionalism.

chapters.title: The Bridge Closes
chapters.summary: Sable, POV. Winter ice closes the bridge; garrison horns announce the occupying delegation will winter in Vellmark pending armistice talks. Sable realizes he cannot leave. Beat: claustrophobia — the trap of staying.

chapters.title: A Girl Named Lene
chapters.summary: Ada (as 'Lene'), POV. Introduce Ada working as a copyist in the occupiers' records office, memorizing which documents get destroyed. She watches her father's name misspelled in a casualty list and corrects nothing. Beat: grief managed through precision.

chapters.title: Inside the Clock
chapters.summary: Sable, POV. Dismantling the master clock's housing, Sable finds a sealed brass cylinder wired into the escapement — Elias Voss's hidden testimony ledger. His hands shake; he recognizes his own childhood handwriting mentioned within. Beat: the past physically lodged in machinery.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Says
chapters.summary: Sable, POV. By candlelight Sable reads the first entries: names, dates, payments — the massacre at the tannery, and the officials who signed off, some now serving the victors. Beat: horror and recognition; he was the boy who saw.

chapters.title: Twelve Years of Quiet
chapters.summary: Sable, POV, flashback woven in. How young Sable witnessed the tannery night and was coached into silence by his mother, who paid for his safety with her own testimony withheld. Beat: understanding that silence was survival, and a debt.

chapters.title: The Keeper's Bargain
chapters.summary: Herr Brandt, POV. Brandt reveals he has guarded the clock and its secret since Voss's death, waiting for someone with skill and no allegiances. He asks Sable to finish what Voss started. Beat: reluctant inheritance.

chapters.title: Lene Reads Over Shoulders
chapters.summary: Ada, POV. In the records office Ada discovers the victors' historians have arrived with pre-drafted histories — Vellmark's chapter already written, exculpatory and blank where the tannery should be. Beat: cold fury.

chapters.title: Two Keepers of Accounts
chapters.summary: Alternating Sable/Ada. They meet properly when Ada comes to the observatory chasing a citation that leads to the clock. Mutual suspicion, then recognition of a fellow keeper of records. Beat: wary alliance formed over shared paper.

chapters.title: The Name Behind Lene
chapters.summary: Ada, POV. Ada confesses her identity to Sable — she is Elias Voss's daughter, hidden in plain sight. Sable does not yet reveal what he found. Beat: trust extended before it is earned.

chapters.title: Authentication
chapters.summary: Sable, POV. To make the ledger admissible they need verification: matching hand, seals, witnesses. Sable begins the delicate forgery-adjacent work of proving a true document true. Beat: meticulous hope.

chapters.title: The Historian Kessler
chapters.summary: Kessler, POV. Introduce the victors' lead historian — not a monster, but a man who believes order requires a clean narrative. He interviews townsfolk gently, filing away inconvenient memories. Beat: menace through courtesy.

chapters.title: Witness One
chapters.summary: Marta Quill, POV. A washerwoman who saw wagons at the tannery agrees to speak — then retracts after a visit from garrison officers. Beat: the cost of memory made visible.

chapters.title: Escapement
chapters.summary: Sable, POV. Repairing the clock becomes metaphor and cover: Sable restores its motion so the observatory stays open, giving them a legitimate reason to meet, copy, and hide documents in plain sight. Beat: purpose crystallizing.

chapters.title: The Armistice Timetable
chapters.summary: Ada, POV. Ada learns the treaty will be signed at midwinter — three weeks — after which all local records pass to Kessler's commission. The deadline is set. Beat: ticking-clock tension begins.

chapters.title: What Sable Withholds
chapters.summary: Ada, POV. Ada senses Sable knows more about the tannery than he admits; confrontation sharpens their partnership into honesty. Sable finally tells her he was there. Beat: rupture and repair.

chapters.title: The Second Cylinder
chapters.summary: Sable, POV. Clues in Voss's ledger point to a second cache — the original sworn depositions — hidden beneath the bridge itself, in the tollhouse foundations. But the bridge is occupied territory now. Beat: the goal moves behind enemy lines.

chapters.title: Kessler Suspects
chapters.summary: Kessler, POV. Kessler notices anomalies: a repaired clock, a copyist's queries, a washerwoman's fear. He begins a quiet counter-investigation. Beat: the hunter wakes.

chapters.title: Midnight Under the Tollhouse
chapters.summary: Sable and Ada, alternating. On a frozen night they reach the tollhouse and find the depositions — but are nearly caught by a patrol; Brandt creates a diversion and is detained. Beat: triumph shadowed by sacrifice.

chapters.title: Brandt in Custody
chapters.summary: Sable, POV. Brandt is held 'for questioning.' Sable must decide whether rescue attempts will expose everything. Brandt, through a bribed guard, tells him: don't come. Beat: guilt versus mission.

chapters.title: The Historian's Doubt
chapters.summary: Kessler, POV. Examining Voss's old files, Kessler finds a discrepancy his own narrative depends on ignoring. For one scene, he wavers. Beat: antagonist humanized; stakes complicated.

chapters.title: Forging a Path to the Record
chapters.summary: Ada, POV. Ada maps how a document could lawfully enter the armistice annex: a neutral signatory, a certified witness, a filing clerk willing to risk everything. Each name is a gamble. Beat: plan assembled from fragile people.

chapters.title: The Filing Clerk
chapters.summary: New character Tomas Rey, POV. A junior occupier clerk who has been quietly misfiling destruction orders for months agrees to help — if the record names his brother, taken in the reprisals. Beat: ally won through shared loss.

chapters.title: Betrayal
chapters.summary: Marta Quill, POV. Terrified and coerced, Marta reveals that documents are moving through the observatory. Kessler now has a thread to pull. Beat: dread; the net tightens.

chapters.title: Raid on the Observatory
chapters.summary: Sable, POV. Soldiers search the tower; Sable hides the depositions inside the clock's restored movement — the one place they'll never dismantle while it runs. The clock literally keeps the truth. Beat: terror transmuted into craft.

chapters.title: Interrogation
chapters.summary: Ada, POV. Ada is brought in for questioning under her false name; Kessler tests her with details only Voss's family would know. She holds. Beat: nerve stretched to breaking.

chapters.title: The Price of the Bridge
chapters.summary: Brandt, POV, from custody. Offered release in exchange for naming his accomplices, Brandt gives Kessler a true but useless answer: 'the clock told me.' Beat: defiance; quiet heroism.

chapters.title: Countdown to Signature
chapters.summary: Tomas Rey, POV. Two days remain. The annex closes early; Kessler requests the signing be moved up. The team must file tonight or never. Beat: acceleration.

chapters.title: Everything Depends on a Seal
chapters.summary: Sable, POV. The depositions lack the certifying seal torn from Voss's office — which Sable realizes was melted into a commemorative medallion Brandt wears, now in the evidence locker. Beat: impossible odds stated plainly.

chapters.title: The Evidence Room
chapters.summary: Ada and Tomas, alternating. Using Tomas's access and a manufactured audit discrepancy, they retrieve the medallion minutes before the room is sealed for the treaty. Beat: heist-tension peak.

chapters.title: Certified
chapters.summary: Sable, POV. In the observatory at dawn, the neutral signatory — an aging Red Cross delegate named Ilse Marren — examines seal, hands, and witnesses, and certifies the record. Beat: trembling legitimacy achieved.

chapters.title: Kessler's Last Card
chapters.summary: Kessler, POV. Kessler discovers the certification and faces a choice: expose it and admit his history is false, or bury it and be complicit in what he condemned. He chooses procedure — and delays the signature by demanding the annex hear testimony. Beat: antagonist's pivot.

chapters.title: The Tribunal at the Custom House
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs briefly. An improvised hearing convenes; Marta, given protection, finally testifies; Tomas enters the misfiled orders. Beat: justice outside the law taking legal form.

chapters.title: Sable Speaks
chapters.summary: Sable, POV. Climax: Sable takes the stand, speaks his full name for the first time in twelve years, and gives eyewitness testimony of the tannery night — ending his mother's bargain and his own invisibility. Beat: catharsis; voice reclaimed.

chapters.title: Signature
chapters.summary: Ada, POV. The certified record is annexed to the armistice minutes as the pen touches paper; Kessler amends his draft rather than falsify against evidence. Beat: victory that feels earned, not triumphant.

chapters.title: Release
chapters.summary: Sable, POV. Brandt walks free, older and lighter; he asks only to see the clock run. Sable shows him the escapement — and the empty space where the truth used to live. Beat: gratitude without sentimentality.

chapters.title: The Bridge Opens
chapters.summary: Ada, POV. Spring thaw; the bridge reopens. Ada signs her real name in the town register for the first time, beside her father's corrected entry. Beat: identity restored.

chapters.title: What the Clock Keeps
chapters.summary: Sable, POV. Sable installs a small plaque inside the clock case naming Elias Voss, visible only to whoever next opens the housing. Some records are for historians; some are for keepers. Beat: memory entrusted forward.

chapters.title: Vellmark, After
chapters.summary: Alternating Sable/Ada, closing. A year later: the town lives with its published record — anger, shame, relief coexisting. Sable takes apprentices; Ada curates the archive. On the observatory steps they agree the hardest work — remembering accurately — has only begun. Beat: resolution with honest, ongoing weight.
